title: The disease of arrogance
hookLine: no one with an atom's weight of arrogance enters the garden, and arrogance is rejecting truth and looking down on people (Muslim)

cards: A gathering in Medina. The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, says that no one with an atom's weight of arrogance in his heart will enter the garden. A man in the room has a worry, and says it out loud.
A man likes his clothes to be good, he says, and his sandals to be good. Is that it? Is a nice pair of sandals what keeps a person out?
It's an honest question, and the answer, recorded in Sahih Muslim, is a definition that fits on a sticky note. Today's word: kibr, arrogance.

teach.h: GOOD SANDALS ARE NOT THE PROBLEM.
teach.b: The answer comes in two halves. First: Allah is beautiful and loves beauty. So the sandals are fine; caring how you look, owning something well made, isn't what the hadith means.
Second, the definition: kibr is rejecting the truth and looking down on people. Two motions of the heart.
Rejecting the truth is hearing something right and pushing it away, because of who said it, or because agreeing would cost face. Looking down on people is treating someone as smaller than you.
Notice what isn't on the list: money, looks, talent. The Qur'an gives a picture of it in Iblis, the one who would not bow, back on day twenty-four.

teach.h: IBLIS: I AM BETTER THAN HIM.
teach.b: His reason is a comparison: I am better than him, you made me from fire and him from clay. Before the refusal, a ranking.

Then Luqman's advice to his son, a father talking to a child: don't turn your cheek away from people in scorn, don't strut on the earth, and, in Pickthall's words, "Lo! Allah loveth not each braggart boaster."
The cheek and the walk: arrogance shows in the body. And the cure for the first half is small. Someone corrects you, and they're right.
You say: you're right. Before the defense, before the but. A sound heart has room in it for being wrong.

how: Muslim teachers count kibr, arrogance, among the diseases of the heart, using the hadith in Sahih Muslim that defines it as rejecting the truth and looking down on people; accepting correction is a common way of working against it.

o: being rich, talented or very good-looking
loving fine clothes, good sandals and nice things
rejecting the truth and looking down on people

games.q: the disease of arrogance — tap the pairs.

s: in the hadith, liking good clothes and sandals is arrogance
the answer was that Allah is beautiful and loves beauty; kibr is rejecting truth and looking down on people.
the hadith's definition of arrogance includes rejecting the truth
kibr is rejecting the truth and looking down on people (Sahih Muslim).
the Qur'an's advice against strutting on the earth is given by Luqman to his son
a father to a child: don't turn your cheek in scorn, don't strut; Allah loveth not each braggart boaster.

games.q: you're in the gathering. a man asks: he likes his clothes and sandals to be good. is that the arrogance just warned about?
o: no: Allah is beautiful and loves beauty; kibr is rejecting truth and looking down on people.
only if they cost a lot.
games.why: the sandals were never the problem. the hadith puts arrogance in two motions of the heart: pushing truth away and looking down on people.

practice: Bring to mind a time someone told you that you were wrong, and they had a point: a coworker, a child, a sibling, a stranger in traffic.
Notice where the pushing away happened, the jaw, the tone, the quick reply, and quietly give the answer you didn't give then: they were right about that.
If you pray, you can ask to be kept from kibr; if you don't, simply rest in the plain fact of it.

wordCard.voice: Kibr. Arrogance; in the hadith, rejecting the truth and looking down on people. Not good sandals. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: arrogance, pride; the word in the hadith in Sahih Muslim.

carryVoice: Your line: reject pride, not truth. Good sandals were never the problem. Tomorrow, a quieter disease: envy.

sources.ref: Sahih Muslim 91 (an atom's weight of arrogance; Allah is beautiful and loves beauty)
